<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-storage`, touching **63** documentable anchor(s).

**53** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 47f6c939f132df9185e1259740e2cbe4156802e1`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `recordId (4 routes)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **42** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 47f6c939f132df9185e1259740e2cbe4156802e1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1c7e625a5fd922169d68e03aad4081cccbdac3e3` — the merge of head `03dcadc63561eba754b2d93991e4877e1473a475` into base `47f6c939f132df9185e1259740e2cbe4156802e1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1c7e625a5fd922169d68e03aad4081cccbdac3e3 && git checkout 1c7e625a5fd922169d68e03aad4081cccbdac3e3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 47f6c939f132df9185e1259740e2cbe4156802e1 03dcadc63561eba754b2d93991e4877e1473a475 && git checkout -B drift-repro 47f6c939f132df9185e1259740e2cbe4156802e1 && git merge --no-ff 03dcadc63561eba754b2d93991e4877e1473a475

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 47f6c939f132df9185e1259740e2cbe4156802e1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 47f6c939f132df9185e1259740e2cbe4156802e1` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `6a6df23affbd19a8d4842f8746eed3e78e005ebd`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

Measured against ruling A (6844223218), #30892 ruling B (a signed-in user, one user, an expiry) and #32686 ruling A (bound ids: same user, that object and field, one record, 1h).

- **Multipart door: right, with one deviation.** `storage-routes.ts` PUT `/upload-links/:token` → `uploadLinkFormFiles` → `RecordFileAccess.consumeUploadLinkFiles`. The ruling B gates are unchanged and still run first: `uploadLinkCaller` gives 401, and `openLink` checks the secret digest, the expiry, `state.user_id === caller` and `owner_id === state.user_id`. The door picks the form arm from the request's `content-type`, not from the link's range. So a one-part form (`count=1`, `file0`) is **accepted** on a single-file field link and on an attachments link. Accepted shape item 2 said that case is refused 400. See ③ F2.
- **Cap: right.** `UPLOAD_LINK_MAX_FILES = 10` (`upload-link-wire.ts`). `refuseFileCount` answers `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`UPLOAD_LINK_FILE_COUNT_*`) in `consumeUploadLinkFiles`. That check runs after `openLink` and before the size checks, the user resolve and the spend. This matches the accepted shape item 3. The mint applies the same cap: `createUploadLinkForNewRecordAs` takes an integer 1–10, and `openLinkStateOf` rejects `reserved_ids.length >= 10`.
- **One spend per submit: right.** There is one `updateFileIfUnchanged(open → used)` per call. Every pre-spend judgement covers all N files: the count, the per-file `uploadSizeRefusal`, `assertFileConstraints` when `newRecord || typed.length > 1`, and `isOpenReservation` for each reserved id.
- **`count` input: right.** MCP `create_upload_link` lists `count` only where `newRecordLinkFn` exists. `count` together with `recordId` is refused before the bridge. The service refuses a non-integer, `<1`, `>10`, and `>1` on a field without `multiple: true`, each `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`. An attachments link cannot carry `count`: without a `recordId` it needs `field`, and with a `recordId` the count arm refuses it.
- **`fileIds` / `fileId` / `files` answer: right, additive.** The raw arm adds `fileIds: [fileId]` and keeps `fileId` and `size`. The form arm answers `fileId` (the first id), `fileIds` (in pick order) and `files[{fileId,size}]`, but no top-level `size` (nit N1). The pre-record mint answers `fileIds: [link.id, ...reserved]`.
- **Reserved rows: right against #32686 A.** Each row is `pending`, owned by the minting user, named `upload-link (reserved)`, has no secret and no record, and carries `kind: upload_link, target: field`. On upload, `filesForNewRecordThroughLink` gives every id the same `preRecordBindingMetadata` (user, object, field, org, `claim_until` = upload + 1h). A failed mint deletes the link row and every reserved row.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset puts `patch` on `@objectstack/service-storage`, `@objectstack/mcp` and `@objectstack/runtime`. These are the three released packages the diff moves; `packages/qa/dogfood` is test-only. With `Metadata-protocol: none`, AGENTS.md §Post-Task 3 calls for `patch`, so the level is right. No `packages/spec` change.
- What the diff publishes is additive only:
  - `McpFileBridge.createUploadLinkForNewRecord` and `McpRecordFileService.createUploadLinkForNewRecordAs` gain an optional `count`;
  - `NewRecordUploadLinkTarget` gains an optional `count`;
  - success answers gain `fileIds`.
  `UploadLinkDoor`, which gains the required `consumeUploadLinkFiles`, is not exported from `service-storage/src/index.ts`, and the only implementer is `FileAttachmentService`. So nothing breaking is published.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right. The accept-set widens: a multi-file link takes N files, a pre-record link takes `count`. The raw-body wire of single-file and attachments links loses no input.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right. No authorable key changes.
- `Skills-docs:` is verified:
  - `git grep` over `skills/` and `ui/skills/` finds no upload-link text;
  - `skill-md.ts` emits the file-tool lines only under `fileTools === true` (`if (options.fileTools !== true) return ''`);
  - the Console mirror `ui/apps/console/src/pages/developer/objectstack-skill.ts` mirrors the no-scope render and has no file or upload text, and `skill-md.test.ts` pins the two renders byte-equal.
  So "the mirror needs no change" holds.
- Changeset and docs sentences vs the code: see F1.

### ③ Boundary flags

Seat conditions:
- **C1, single-file and attachments links unchanged: holds on the raw-body wire.** `consumeUploadLink` delegates with `[upload]`. The order is unchanged: open, then filename, then bytes, then size (413), then the user resolve (403), then the pre-record constraints, then the spend. The count check cannot refuse one file on a range that admits 1. The added pre-spend `accept`/`maxSize` runs only when `typed.length > 1`. No refusal code or status changes for a raw PUT. The multipart wire on these links changed: see F2.
- **C2, reserved ids before upload: holds.**
  - Writes: the uploader's own write hits the `applyCopyOnClaim` incomplete-upload arm (`!isCompletedUpload`). Another user's write, and a system or context-less write (`writerUserId === null`), get `not_yours` from `preRecordReferenceRefusal`, because the row's metadata satisfies `isPreRecordLinkRow`. The system lookup `findReferenceableFile` reaches the row.
  - Reads: the download door refuses a `pending` row (`isServableForDownload`), and `isUploaderOnlyFile` denies others. `readRecordFileAs` reads only ids the record holds, and no write can make a record hold a reserved id.
  - Not a link: `openLinkStateOf` requires `name === 'upload-link'` and `secret_sha256`. A reserved row has neither, so it never opens, and the pin uses the real secret.
  - Reaping: the `sys_file` retention (`status: pending`, 7d) reaps it.
- **C3, partial failure after spend: holds.**
  - Record link: `fillFieldThroughLink` tracks `created` and `stored` per file, writes the field once (`[...current, ...ids]`), and on any throw discards every file it created.
  - Pre-record link: `filesForNewRecordThroughLink` discards every id, including rows not yet reached (`bytesStored = i < stored`).
  - The tests pin a store failure on file 2 for both link kinds, and a 409 lock after the spend.

Break attempts:
- **Multipart on a single-file or attachments link:** 2 or more parts give `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` before the spend. A malformed form gives `400 INVALID_REQUEST` before `openLink`. A one-part form lands and spends the link (F2).
- **Duplicated, reordered or missing parts:** the door reads exactly `file0…file{count-1}`. Every file-valued entry, and every key matching `/^file\d+$/`, must total `count`. A non-file `fileN` or a missing index is refused. A repeated name collapses in the parser and then mismatches `count`. Order follows the index. No more than N files are stored, and no uncounted file is stored.
- **accept/maxSize before spend:** yes for every file of an N>1 submit and of every pre-record submit. A one-file record submit is judged by the record write after the spend, as before (C1).
- **A second user claiming an id:** refused. `openLink` rejects the stranger (404, nothing spent, pinned). Their write naming an id gets `not_yours`, both before and after the upload. A system write naming an unheld bound id also gets `not_yours`.
- **`count` range:** validated at the MCP schema (`int().min(1)`) and in the service (1–10). Refused above 1 on a single-file field. Not accepted on an attachments link.
- **Locales:** all 11 `CopyLocale` tables carry all six new keys (`wantedSeveral`, `wantedExactly`, `filesLabel`, `attachedSeveral`, `receivedSeveral`, `pickCount`). `Record<CopyLocale, UploadLinkCopy>` makes them compiler-required, and `upload-link-copy.test.ts` pins them non-empty and carrying the number.
- **Ablations (12 reported), judged from the code:** each of the 12 mutations reaches an assertion that the pin makes. The guards that no pin covers:
  - the pre-spend `isOpenReservation` loop;
  - the `openLinkStateOf` `reserved_ids` shape check (no duplicate or self-id check, N2);
  - the form-arm declared cap `formLimit`;
  - the one-part form on a one-file link.
- **Body cap `maxUploadBytes × 10 + 64 KiB`: checked on the parsed form in the PUT handler, so it is not a pre-read guard for this door.** `uploadLinkFormFiles` then copies every part to a `Buffer`, for any `count` up to 999, before the service's count check (F3).

Dev flags (PR body Acceptance notes; os-dev-report 6864752482):
- C1–C3, Q1 (exact `count`), Q2 (attachments stay one file) and the mirror claim are confirmed as above, except for F2 under C1.
- The "other one-file wording read" claim holds for the touched surfaces.
- The report's `security_findings: "withheld"` carries no content on the card. Not judged here.

Check-runs at head (50 read): 25 success, 15 skipped, 10 in progress (`Test Core` 1–8/8, `Type Check · workspace`, `Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus`), 0 failure. `Dogfood Regression Gate` succeeded, but its shard jobs were skipped. This verdict is on the contract only; the gate verdict is still pending.

Findings:
- **F1, should-fix:** `.changeset/32747-upload-link-multiple-files.md` ¶2 and `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx` (multi-file paragraph) say every file of a send is checked against `accept`/`maxSize` before the spend, and that a refused file leaves the link usable. For a one-file send on a multi-file record link, the check happens in the record write after the spend, so the link is spent. Narrow both to "a send of more than one file, or a link for a record not yet created".
- **F2, should-fix:** `storage-routes.ts` PUT handler, form arm chosen by `isUploadLinkForm(content-type)`. A one-part form on a single-file or attachments link is admitted, and its declared cap widens from `maxUploadBytes` to `10× + 64 KiB`. This deviates from accepted-shape item 2 and is unpinned. Either refuse a form on a link whose range max is 1, before the spend, or amend the shape and pin the behaviour.
- **F3, should-fix:** `uploadLinkFormFiles` and the comment "refused before it is read". The form cap is not a pre-buffer guard, and the door materialises up to 999 parts. Bound `count` to `UPLOAD_LINK_MAX_FILES` before any `arrayBuffer()`, and correct the comment.
- **N1, nit:** the form-arm answer has no top-level `size`, while the raw arm has one.
- **N2, nit:** `openLinkStateOf` does not reject duplicate `reserved_ids`, or one equal to the link id. That is reachable only through the owner's own row metadata, and it can orphan bytes in their own scope.
- **N3, nit:** `discard(..., bytesStored = false)` no longer deletes the key of the file whose `storage.upload` threw. On `main` the single-file path did delete it. Bytes from a partial adapter write can be left.
- **N4, nit:** the MCP `count` schema has no `.max(10)`. The description states the cap, and the service refuses above it.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-4i7bf9`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L9qibzuZJBQY4wUQFJbkfx`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `5cc654121039c794c8998b72f823f8397334752a`
Local-runs: none

Round 2 is a delta review: `501eafef..5cc65412`, plus `6a6df23a..501eafef` read as round-1 context, plus the whole net diff against `main` (merge-base `128b6571`, unchanged) for the narrowing question. Labels: **F** = must-fix (FAIL), **S** = should-fix, **N** = nit. Round-1 ids appear as r1-F1…r1-N4.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The door's path choice: right for one-file links, wrong on main's multi-file field links (F-1).** For a `multipart/form-data` body, the door now asks the link first (`storage-routes.ts:1899-1900` → `severalFilesOf` `:2472-2484`, `inspectUploadLink`, which does a read and writes nothing). Only `files.max > 1` (`:2483`) reads the form. A single-file field link, an attachments link, or a link for a record not yet created with `count: 1` takes the raw body (`:1936-1946`). That path has main's declared cap (`:1914`) and main's order. This answers the coordinator's round-1 ask for one-file links. But a `multiple: true` field's record link existed on `main` and took any body as its one file (main `storage-routes.ts:1890-1905`). It now parses every multipart body as the indexed form (F-1).
- **The cap (10, `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`): right, unchanged.** The door now also refuses `count > linkFiles.max` before reading any part (`:2536`). Both refusals share one spelling, `uploadLinkFileCountMessage` (`upload-link-wire.ts`).
- **One spend per submit: right, unchanged** (`record-file-access.ts:1210`).
- **Pre-spend `accept`/`maxSize`: widened to every send on a link that takes several** (`record-file-access.ts:1192`, `newRecord || range.max > 1`). A one-file raw send to a multi-file field's record link is now judged before the spend, and the link stays usable. The refusal code and status are the ones the record write answered on `main`, but its precedence moved (S-1).
- **`count` input: right.** MCP now declares `.max(10)` (`mcp-http-tools.ts:3431`, pinned). The service range is unchanged.
- **`fileIds` / `fileId` / `files`: right, additive.** The one-file raw answer is main's plus `fileIds` (`storage-routes.ts:1955-1961`). The form answer still has no top-level `size` (`:1927-1933`, N-1).
- **Reserved rows: unchanged since round 1.** They still hold against #32686 A.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `service-storage`, `mcp` and `runtime` with `Metadata-protocol: none`: right. Nothing new is exported.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is **not accurate while F-1 stands**. A request `main` accepted is now refused 400: a `multipart/form-data` body sent to a usable `multiple: true` field's record link, when the body is not the indexed form. If F-1 is kept rather than fixed, the PR body and changeset must declare `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, with the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 disposition (AGENTS.md §Post-Task 3).
- `Skills-docs:`: unchanged and still true. The Console mirror stays no-scope.
- The changeset's last paragraph and `connect-mcp.mdx:306` now match the code for single-file and attachments links, and for "however many" on multi-file links.

### ③ Boundary flags

(a) **Can a one-file link refuse or reorder anything main answered?** No, for a single-file field link, an attachments link, or a `count: 1` link.
- The order is 401 (`:1877`), then a missing door 404 (`:1881`), then a side-effect-free inspect, then the declared 413 against `maxUploadBytes` (`:1914`), then `rawBody` (`:1938`), then `consumeUploadLink` (`:1946`). That is main's sequence, with an inspect read added that never answers.
- When inspect throws (expired, used, another user's, unknown, no engine), `catch → undefined` (`:2480`) takes the raw path, so 413 still precedes 404, as on `main`.
- In the service, a one-file send on these links passes the count check (`record-file-access.ts:1156`). Constraint judgement stays in the record write (`:1192`, `range.max === 1`).
- The only answer change is the added `fileIds`. Outside this set, F-1 and S-1 concern `multiple: true` field links, which also took one file per use on `main`.

(b) **Can the inspect read be raced into a wrong path?** No, in a way that matters.
- A one-file link takes the raw path whatever the race does.
- A multi-file link spent or expired between inspect and spend reaches `openLink` inside `consumeUploadLinkFiles`, which answers main's `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`. The conditional spend (`:1210`) still allows exactly one use.
- The residual: a racing multi-file multipart body declared between `max` and `max × N` answers 404 where main answered 413. Both are refusals of a used link. N-level, not filed.

(c) **Round-1 items**
- r1-F1: resolved, by a code change and docs. The changeset ¶2 and `connect-mcp.mdx:306` now match `record-file-access.ts:1192`; see S-1 for its cost.
- r1-F2: superseded by the coordinator's ruling. A one-file link takes the body raw (a).
- r1-F3: resolved at this door. The cap is `maxUploadBytes × linkFiles.max + 64 KiB` (`storage-routes.ts:1902-1905`). `count > max` and every part-shape refusal return before any `arrayBuffer()` (`:2530-2556` vs `:2564`). Pinned with counted reads (`record-file-access.integration.test.ts:1525`). The comment at `:1884-1893` is now accurate.
- r1-N3: resolved. `attempted` is set before `storage.upload` (`record-file-access.ts:1275`, `:1383`), and `discard` deletes a key whose upload was tried (`:1436`). Pinned (`…integration.test.ts:1424`).
- r1-N4: resolved (`mcp-http-tools.ts:3431`, pinned).
- r1-N1: still open (N-1).
- r1-N2: still open (N-2, `record-file-access.ts:568-571`).

(d) **Is the new pin genuine?** Yes.
- `…integration.test.ts:1490-1512`: for both link kinds, a multipart body declared at 1 MiB + 1 under a 1 MiB limit gets 413 with main's `uploadSizeRefusal` words (`:1501`). Under the limit it is stored with its own length (`:1506`). The link's second use gets 404 (`:1508`).
- The ablation is genuine. If every link reads a form, the cap becomes 1 MiB + 64 KiB, which exceeds the declared length, so there is no 413. `useLink` carries no `body`, so `uploadLinkFormFiles({})` answers `400 INVALID_REQUEST` (`storage-routes.ts:2530`). The pin goes red at `:1501`.
- The pin does not cover the inspect-throws fallback (S-2).

**PR body (rewritten) vs code.**
- "What changes" and Acceptance C1 match the code for single-file and attachments links. Acceptance line 114 discloses the multi-file pre-spend judgement.
- Line 112, "no narrowing of existing links", is false while F-1 stands.
- Line 24 ("a one-file send takes the same steps in the same order as before") contradicts lines 30 and 114 for multi-file links.
- The case counts "13 cases" (lines 17 and 56) are stale (N-3).

**Check-runs at head (57 read):** 40 success, 17 skipped, 0 failure, 0 in progress. `Test Core` 1–8/8 and `Type Check · workspace` are success. `Dogfood Regression Gate` succeeded, but its shard jobs were skipped, so CI did not run the touched dogfood file.

Findings:
- **F-1, must-fix: narrowing on `main`'s multi-file field links.** `storage-routes.ts:1899-1900`, `:2483`, `:1920`, `:2530`. A usable `multiple: true` field's record link that receives a `multipart/form-data` body answers `400 INVALID_REQUEST` (or `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` for a `count` it does not take) whenever the body is not `count` plus `file0…`. On `main` (`storage-routes.ts:1890-1905`) that same link stored the body as its one file, subject to the field's `accept`. This is the class the coordinator ruled a narrowing in round 1, now on the links that existed on `main`. The page never sends such a body, but neither did it in round 1. Cure one of three ways:
  - (i) the page marks its several-file send with its own header, and a multipart body without the header keeps main's raw path on every link;
  - (ii) keep main's raw path when the parsed form carries no `count`;
  - (iii) declare `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` with the BREAKING banner, the ADR-0087 disposition, and a pin.
- **S-1, should-fix (disclosed, PR body line 114): refusal precedence moved for a one-file send on a multi-file field's record link.** `record-file-access.ts:1192` judges `accept`/`maxSize` before the spend. On `main` the same judgement ran inside the record write (main `:970` was `if (newRecord)` only). When the file also meets a spend race (404), a `RECORD_NOT_FOUND`, a `readonlyWhen` strict refusal or a lock, the answer is now `400 ERR_FILE_CONSTRAINT` where `main` answered the other refusal. No request main accepted is refused here, and the link stays usable (a widening). Either the coordinator accepts this explicitly as the r1-F1 cure under ruling A, or the code reverts to `typed.length > 1` and the docs are narrowed instead.
- **S-2, should-fix: the inspect-throws fallback is unpinned.** `storage-routes.ts:2480`. Rethrowing there instead of `return undefined` stays green: the pin's used-link step (`…integration.test.ts:1508`) declares no length and answers 404 either way. Add the case: a used or expired one-file link, a multipart body declared over the limit, expecting 413 with main's words.
- **N-1, nit (r1-N1):** the form answer has no top-level `size` (`storage-routes.ts:1927-1933`).
- **N-2, nit (r1-N2):** `openLinkStateOf` accepts duplicate `reserved_ids`, or one equal to the link id (`record-file-access.ts:568-571`).
- **N-3, nit:** PR body: "13 cases" (lines 17 and 56) are stale, and line 24 overstates "same steps in the same order" for multi-file links.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-4i7bf9`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L9qibzuZJBQY4wUQFJbkfx`

**VERDICT: CHANGES**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `03dcadc63561eba754b2d93991e4877e1473a475`
